title: Probe-trace-assisted failure classification to inform autoscaler actions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Current autoscaler decisions rely on aggregated probe pass/fail rates and coarse health scores which conflate multiple failure modes (CPU saturation, GC pause, KV-cache pressure, network queueing). This leads to oscillation and incorrect scale actions: unnecessary scale-ups for transient GC spikes or missed scale-ups when tail queueing causes degraded SLOs.

Goal: Use distributed request traces correlated with readiness/liveness probe failures to classify the dominant failure mode per instance/region and surface a low-latency classifier score to the autoscaler. The classifier will inform three mutually exclusive autoscaler actions: scale-up, progressive load-shed (route-level), or mark for graceful draining and replacement. We want to reduce autoscaler thrash while improving SLO preservation during multi-region incidents and regional failovers.
technical_design:
High-level pipeline:
1) Probe-trace joiner: enrich probe events with the most recent trace span(s) for that instance (last 30s window). Instrument lightweight trace IDs on synthetic canaries and high-error tokens to increase signal.
2) Feature extraction: produce a fixed feature vector from traces and probes: recent p50/p95 latency gaps, active request queue depth, kernel scheduling stalls from host metrics, GC pause fraction, mean inference tokens-in-flight, probe failure pattern (gradual vs immediate), and region token weight.
3) Classifier: a small ensemble (decision tree + logistic fallback) trained on historical labeled incidents (rollback/pgdump/rv) to return a failure-mode label and confidence: {cpu, gc, queueing, network, kernel, unknown}. Implement inference as a C++ microservice collocated with the telemetry agent for sub-100ms scoring.
4) Autoscaler integration: add a decision plane endpoint that accepts instance classifier outputs and returns action suggestions. Action mapping rules: high-confidence queueing -> scale-up/burst; high-confidence GC/kernel -> mark for drain+replace; low-confidence or unknown with rising tail latency -> progressive routing shed (token-weighted).
5) Observability: expose classifier score histograms, feature distributions, and per-action audit traces in Console. Provide a reversible feature-flag gate and per-route aggressiveness knobs.

Impl notes and constraints:
- Classifier must be memory-light and fail-open (return unknown) if telemetry backlog spikes.
- Avoid adding tail latency; scoring should be async and cached for 5s.
- Respect tenant isolation: do not leak tenant IDs in any exported dashboards; use hashed IDs for per-tenant analysis.
- Start with region-local decisioning; central coordinator only for aggregated dashboards, not for fast path decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end pipeline deployed to staging: probe-trace joiner, featurizer, classifier, and autoscaler decision endpoint.
2) Classifier latency median < 40ms (p95 < 120ms) on service machines.
3) In a staged load test with injected queueing faults, feature-flagged cluster shows 30% fewer inappropriate scale-ups and a 20% improvement in tail latency SLO compared to control.
4) Console surfaces per-region classifier metrics and an audit log showing autoscaler decisions with classifier rationale.
5) Rollout plan validated: can disable per-route aggressiveness without restart; feature flag respected across Dedicated and Private deployments.
6) Security review performed for telemetry retention and PII handling (hashed tenant ids).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for featurizer and classifier logic.
- Integration tests: synthetic canary scenarios (GC spike, CPU spin, injected queueing via load generator) in staging using the incident-sim harness.
- Chaos test: Gradual crash/drain simulation across a region while classifier-enabled autoscaler operates; compare failover latency to baseline.
- A/B experiment in non-critical region: 50% of requests routed to cluster with classifier-based autoscaler for 2 weeks, gather SLO, cost, and scale events.
- Perf regression test added to CI with a baseline p95 classifier latency threshold.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag behind 'probe_trace_classifier' gate. Enable in staging for 1 week and run synthetic incident scenarios.
2) Canary rollout to 'eu-west-2' non-prod region for 72h; monitor classifier score quality and autoscaler actions.
3) Gradual expansion to low-traffic prod routes (10%, 30%, 100%) over two weeks with rollback playbook.
4) If any increase in costly scale-ups or regression to SLO, immediately disable feature flag and trigger oncall runbook.
5) Post-mortem after full prod rollout to capture classifier failures and retraining dataset.

comments: 2025-02-20: Kickoff meeting with reliability and infra teams. Agreed to keep scoring local to avoid central latency. - Aisha
2025-02-25: Design review completed; noted need for per-tenant hashing to avoid PII exposure. Action: add telemetry retention policy. - Jae

2025-02-28: Initial probe-trace joiner prototype pushed to feature branch: github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/compare/probe-joiner. Observed initial memory overhead ~12MB per agent; within budget. - Jae

2025-03-03: Perf run in staging with synthetic queueing fault. Classifier p50=28ms p95=95ms. False-positive rate for GC classification 8% in pilot dataset. Need more labeled GC incidents to retrain. - Reliability QA
2025-03-05: Opened PR for autoscaler decision API integration: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/409. Requesting review from @maria-nguyen and @liam-cole. - Jae
